narrative: OMX30 faces headwinds this morning with global equity markets printing red across Europe, Americas and Asia-Pacific, driven by mixed macro signals and profit-taking. The index sits in an awkward technical position: still +4.0% above the 200-day moving average suggesting underlying bull structure, but -1.0% below the 50-day MA and MACD rolling over below signal line indicate near-term momentum has stalled. ADX strength at 52.6 with bearish directional bias confirms sellers have control, though RSI at 30.24 approaches oversold territory, creating mean-reversion risk if selling exhausts. The weighted correlation signal of -0.384% reinforces a risk-off day, though stronger USD/SEK (+0.69%) provides tactical support for large-cap exporters. Watch for any stabilisation at the lower Bollinger Band around 3085 or risk extension toward 3050 if sentiment deteriorates further.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to selling pressure tracking broad European weakness (DAX -22bp, CAC -37bp, FTSE -36bp) with Hang Seng's 100bp drop signalling risk-off contagion from Asia. Technical picture is decidedly bearish: MACD negative histogram at -11.357, ADX 52.6 with sell bias, price action firmly in lower half of Bollinger Bands (%B 0.04). RSI 30.24 flags mean-reversion risk but insufficient conviction yet to call a bounce. Key support sits at 3085 (lower BB) with 3123 (yesterday close) as near-term pivot; resistance remains 3150-3180 (50-MA zone). Industrials and Tech face headwinds from oil weakness and NASDAQ -56bp spillover, but Banks may stabilise on yield resilience (US 10Y 4.96%) and exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) should watch USD/SEK strength (+69bp). US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET offers potential volatility trigger. Trade cautiously, expect -0.1% to -0.4% range; breach of 3085 targets 3050.
